title: devcontainer-kit per-repository config (.devcontainer/dck.toml), interface 2
description: TOML document, described here as its JSON equivalent. Unknown keys are ignored with a warning.

interface.description: 2; a version-1 file is read for migration only (dck init rewrites it)

service.description: Compose service the tools attach to

workspace.description: workspaceFolder (the app path): the repository mount and where every Herdr workspace and new pane opens

image_tag.description: interface 1 only: ignored since v0.2.0 (no shared base image); dck init removes it

ssh_port.description: Loopback-only host port for the container sshd (Herdr); 0 = no sshd. A string is the host port as a compose expression ("${SSH_PORT:-22540}"); the container port is always 22

bind.description: Host address every published port binds to

ports.description: Named ports: an integer is published as <bind>:<port>:<port>; a string ("HOST:CONTAINER", each a number or ${VAR:-default}) verbatim after <bind>: unless it names a host IP

agents.description: Install coding-agents-kit (ak) at its pinned tag

dailybot.description: Install the Dailybot CLI (only when the dailybot addon asks for it)

editor.description: nvim + deepworkplan-vim as the default editor

clis.description: The CLIs installed (and, without supported, wired) when layers.agents is true ([] = none). With supported (advanced), the default set each developer can change (DCK_AGENT_CLIS, INSTALL_<CLI>_CLI, the host profile's [agents] clis / clis_extra); must be within supported

supported.description: Advanced: the CLIs every image is wired for, installed or not (home volumes, host-profile sharing, default_profile); each developer chooses what to install within them. "all" = every kind ak knows. Unset (the default): clis — wire and install the CLIs chosen at onboarding

presets.description: ak alias presets turned on; absent = classic and providers (as before v0.3.3); new renders write []

node_first.description: put the agents' own Node (/opt/dck/node, installed when the image's node is older than the pinned major) first on PATH for every process and login shell, for a repository whose own tooling needs it; off: the image's node stays first

state_volume.description: the named volume of this service's state (sshd host key, ~/.ssh, gh auth, Herdr client state, history), mounted at ~/.dck/volumes/state; give each repository its own when several share one compose project; not an agents-layer volume name

project.description: the rendered top-level compose project name (default <compose_project_prefix><repo-slug>); wins over COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME in the environment or the compose .env (dck passes -p)

networks.description: existing external networks; merged with the host profile's network and x-dck-merge.networks into one top-level networks: (external: true)

volumes.description: extra compose-managed volumes declared with their exact names (<project>_<name>, so the data volumes of the file's other services keep reattaching); or declare them in the user:volumes sub-block

machine.description: Register the container as a Herdr machine on `dck up` (needs ssh_port)

layout.description: the Herdr sidebar dck up creates inside the container

mesh.description: dck up runs dck herdr mesh (Docker Desktop only): agents inside reach the other dck containers and, with host_machine, the host

base_image.description: optional: an official image for the runtime, pinned by digest; defaults to the flavour's pin in versions.env

ssh_agent.description: share the host's SSH agent with the container (git over SSH; keys never enter it)

ssh_host_config.description: dck up makes the host's ~/.ssh/config aliases (public keys only) usable inside; needs ssh_agent

context.description: build context relative to the compose file's directory (default ./<service>); the Dockerfile and dck/ paths are computed relative to it

dockerfile.description: a Dockerfile shared by several services, relative to the repository (default docker/local/<service>/Dockerfile); dck's managed blocks and its dck/ directory go next to it

dev_sh.description: false: dck init neither creates nor touches dev.sh (a repository that keeps its own); dck init --no-dev-sh writes it
